name: GARCH (and ARCH)
summary: Models time-varying volatility: today's variance depends on recent shocks and recent variance.
inputs: A return series (not prices), typically daily.
outputs: Conditional volatility path, volatility forecasts, VaR and expected-shortfall inputs.

data_requirements.missing_values: Drop non-trading days; do not fill returns

assumptions: Returns have (near) zero conditional mean or a modelled mean
Volatility clusters: today's variance depends on past squared shocks and past variance
Chosen innovation distribution (normal, Student-t) is adequate
math_summary: sigma_t^2 = omega + sum alpha_i e_{t-i}^2 + sum beta_j sigma_{t-j}^2, with e_t = sigma_t z_t. ARCH (Engle) uses only past squared shocks; GARCH (Bollerslev) adds lagged conditional variance.
when_to_use: Daily or intraday return series with volatility clustering
when_not_to_use: When leverage or asymmetry matters and you only fit symmetric GARCH (use EGARCH/GJR)
pitfalls: Persistence alpha+beta near 1 can signal structural breaks rather than true long memory

compute.complexity: Maximum likelihood, O(n) per likelihood evaluation.

applicability.use_case: Daily volatility and VaR for FX rates
